title: Stacks
summary: Last in, first out: the right tool for undo, nesting and matching pairs.

sections.heading: Last in, first out
body: A stack is a pile: you add to the top and take from the top. A plain array or list is all you need: `push`/`append` to add, `pop` to take the newest item.

javascript.code:
const stack = []
stack.push('a')
stack.push('b')
stack.push('c')
console.log(stack.pop())
console.log(stack)

typescript.code:
const stack: string[] = []
stack.push('a')
stack.push('b')
stack.push('c')
console.log(stack.pop())
console.log(stack)

python.code:
stack = []
stack.append('a')
stack.append('b')
stack.append('c')
print(stack.pop())
print(stack)

sections.heading: Undo, and anything that nests
body: Undo removes the most recent action, which is exactly what `pop` does.
Nesting works the same way. When something opens (a bracket, a tag), push it. When something closes, pop and check it matches. At the end, the stack should be empty.

mistakes: Popping an empty stack: JavaScript gives `undefined`, Python raises `IndexError`. Check the length first.
Forgetting to check that the stack is empty at the end (something was opened but never closed).
